notes: The complete conditional implication is valid. The supplied product-cover route handles n=0 separately, removes zero-diameter obstructions when n≥1, controls every scale, and takes the final finite-dimensional order limit. Only H002, the stated N001/N002 premises, definitions, and the routine facts reviewed below are used; no producer proof or external theorem is required.

applicability.notes: N001 applies to E⊆Eucl(n) with q>D≥0, and to F⊆Eucl(n+1) with exponents a>1 or q+1>0. N002 supplies finiteness and nonnegativity of D. All ball, power, series and infimum facts have their actual local conditions verified in BG001–BG007. There are no E/M applications.

argument.notes: For n=0 the interval partitions have mesh and a-cost tending to zero. For n≥1 the singleton replacements preserve coverage with the stated summable budget; the ceiling partition gives at most 2/r_i product pieces, each of diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i. Their (q+1)-cost is bounded by the stated constant times epsilon. Sending the cost tolerance to zero at each fixed scale, then taking the supremum over scales, proves H^{q+1}(F)=0. The final q↓D order argument proves exactly N003.

dependency_closure.notes: H002 is used in the n=0 branch; N001 and N002 are used exactly as stated. U is chosen only after F002 establishes its existence; r_i>0 makes every ceiling and division legitimate. The arbitrary r,epsilon cover witnesses are eliminated in F004, whose statement retains only q. L3 is discharged before quantifying q, L2 is discharged after the bound is independent of q, and the exhaustive natural-number cases close the proof. No witness or branch assumption escapes.

packet_replay.notes: The packet suffices for the conditional proof using its full direct-input statements, D001–D008 and the positively checked local background notes. No missing fact from an input producer, source paper, other R, or additional original hypothesis is needed. This judges mathematical sufficiency only.

statement_closure.notes: The ambient Euclidean identification and product metric, extended diameter, positive-exponent contents, dimension convention, interval I, F and D are supplied. N002 authorizes real arithmetic with finite D. Quantifiers over q, scales and tolerances and the countable-cover witnesses are explicit; F004 removes private cover names. The exported statement is the unconditional extended-dimension inequality dimH(F)≤D+1, with no added restriction on n or E.

background_notes.fact: For b>0, x↦x^b on nonnegative real numbers is increasing, tends to zero as x↓0, and satisfies (cx)^b=c^b x^b for c,x>0. For a>1, N^{1-a}→0 as positive integers N→∞, and 1/N→0.

grounds.reason: The interval exponent satisfies a>1 and N is a positive integer.
N002 and q>D give q>0, hence q+1>0; the replacement radii are positive.

background_notes.justification: These are the elementary real-power laws and limits: for x>0 write x^b=exp(b log x). Increasing log and exp give monotonicity and the product law; log x→−∞ at zero gives the first limit. Since N^{1-a}=(1/N)^{a-1}, the integer limit follows. The uses at zero respect 0^b=0 for b>0.

background_notes.fact: In Eucl(n) with n≥1, a closed ball B(x,rho) of radius rho>0 is nonempty and has diameter 2rho. For any r,eta>0 and q>0 there is such a ball centered at x with 0<diam(B)≤r and diam(B)^q<eta. A nonempty Euclidean set of diameter zero is a singleton.

grounds.reason: The branch assumes n≥1, q>0 has already been derived, and r,epsilon are positive; each zero-diameter covering member is nonempty after empty members are discarded.
The ambient metric is the Euclidean distance on real n-tuples.
Diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances.

background_notes.justification: The triangle inequality bounds all ball distances by 2rho; the two points x±rho e_1 lie in the ball and attain this value. Choose rho sufficiently small that 2rho≤r and (2rho)^q<eta, using BG001. If diam A=0, all distances between its points vanish, so any chosen point is its only point. This validates precisely the singleton replacements already displayed in S002.

background_notes.fact: For a nonnegative extended-real infimum h=inf C, if h=0 then for every eta>0 some c∈C satisfies c<eta. Conversely, if for every eta>0 C contains a member of cost below eta, then inf C=0. For the contents defined in D003, H^s(A)=0 implies H^s_delta(A)=0 for each delta>0; if every positive-scale content is zero then H^s(A)=0.

grounds.reason: Each content is an infimum of nonnegative countable-cover costs; the measure is their supremum over positive scales.
N001 gives H^q(E)=0, so S002 uses zero scale content with eta=epsilon/2.
At every fixed scale the displayed interval covers eventually become admissible and have costs tending to zero.
F004 supplies admissible covers at fixed delta with costs below C e0, for every e0>0, where C=2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) is positive and finite.

background_notes.justification: If no c<eta existed, eta would be a positive lower bound, contradicting inf C=0. Conversely any positive proposed infimum is contradicted by choosing a smaller positive tolerance. Nonnegativity then gives equality to zero. Every scale content is bounded above by their supremum. Supremum of a family of zeros is zero. In S005 choose e0=eta/C, so no exchange of limits or infima is involved.

background_notes.fact: For 0<t≤1, the integer m=ceil(1/t) is positive and satisfies 1/m≤t and m≤1/t+1≤2/t. A countable union of finite families is countable. If diam U=t and J is an interval of length at most t, then the Euclidean product U×J has diameter at most sqrt(2)t.

grounds.reason: The chosen cover is countable and has 0<r_i≤r≤1.
N_i is defined by the ceiling and each subinterval has length 1/N_i.
Squared product distance is the sum of the squared coordinate distances.

background_notes.justification: The ceiling lies between 1/t and 1/t+1; reciprocation of positive numbers gives 1/m≤t. Countable pairs (i,j), 0≤j<N_i, form a subset of a countable Cartesian product. Pairwise product distances are bounded by sqrt(t²+t²), hence their supremum is bounded by sqrt(2)t. These facts justify the finite partitions and countability used in S003.

background_notes.fact: Countable sums of nonnegative extended-real terms admit termwise comparison and regrouping over countable partitions. Also sum_{i≥0}2^{−i−2}=1/2. Consequently the singleton replacements in S002 cost at most epsilon/2, and the grouping of product-cover costs in S004 is valid before finiteness is established.

grounds.reason: Each replacement has q-cost below epsilon 2^{−i−2}; all costs are nonnegative and the original cover costs less than epsilon/2.
W is indexed by the countable original family with finite fibers of size N_i.
Each fiber cost is bounded by N_i(sqrt(2)r_i)^{q+1} and sum_i r_i^q<epsilon.

background_notes.justification: A nonnegative countable sum is the supremum of its finite subsums. Comparing finite subsums proves comparison; finite subsets of a countably partitioned index set give equality with the iterated sums by taking these suprema. The geometric-series partial sums here are (1/2)(1−2^{−m}), tending to 1/2. The strict original epsilon/2 bound plus the non-strict replacement epsilon/2 bound yields total cost strictly below epsilon. The same comparison and regrouping give exactly the displayed S004 estimate.

background_notes.fact: If d is a finite nonnegative real number and X∈[0,infinity] satisfies X≤d+1+1/j for every positive integer j, then X≤d+1. Likewise X≤a for every real a>1 implies X≤1.

grounds.reason: D is finite and nonnegative.
Discharged F005 gives the bound for every q>D, in particular q=D+1/j.
The n=0 argument gives dimH(F)≤a for every a>1.

background_notes.justification: A single finite upper bound excludes X=infinity. If the finite X exceeded d+1, choose j with 1/j<X−(d+1) using the Archimedean property, contradicting the assumed bound. For the second claim take a=1+1/j. This checks both final order limits without assuming dimension was already finite.

background_notes.fact: For delta>0, r_star=min(1,delta/sqrt(2)) lies in (0,1] and sqrt(2)r_star≤delta. The positive finite constant 2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) depends on the fixed q alone.

grounds.reason: delta is arbitrary positive and q remains fixed while e0 decreases to zero.
F004 is universally quantified over r0∈(0,1] and e0>0.

background_notes.justification: Both entries in the minimum are positive. Its two defining upper bounds give r_star≤1 and r_star≤delta/sqrt(2). Multiplication by sqrt(2)>0 gives the desired mesh. Positivity and finiteness of the constant allow arbitrary cost tolerances at this fixed mesh.
